quest.title: Tread the Right Path
quest.description: After waking from her dream, Linnea decides to seek Celaeno out once more and uncover the whole truth.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Primogem x60, Mora x53900, Guide to Vagrancy x5, Spirit Envoy Championship Champion Medal x1, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Linnea! You're awake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were out for a long time. You must be starving! Do you want something to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Linnea? Wh—Why are you crying?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: What time is it? I...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's evening... Uh, and it's the day after the quarterfinals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were watching the match between Celaeno and Jahoda, when you ran over and grabbed Celaeno's arm. Then, you just passed out. Do you have any recollection?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: So many things came flooding into my head, one after another... The end of the competition, things from my future... Even the very end of my life, when I finally had to bid farewell to the world...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Some moments were joyful, others painful... All of it felt so, so real. I don't know how to describe it, but... it was terrifying.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (After one of her matches, Linnea mentioned her mysterious intuition that helps her predict her opponent's moves.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Celaeno seemed to display a similar ability during her match with Jahoda. Could this have something to do with Linnea's dream?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good point — you passed out right after grabbing her. Plus, she said a load of cryptic-sounding stuff... She has to know something about what's going on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still... Is it really a good idea to go looking for her? What if the same thing happens again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, it could trigger more of those vivid dreams...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Do you remember when we were at Speranza, and I told you guys about my childhood? Well... There were a few details I left out.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: I wasn't a very cheerful kid, nor was I all that brave. Before I told my human parents about being a fae, I spent so many sleepless nights tossing and turning.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: I knew what might happen once I told them. I desperately hoped they'd say, "Linnea, even if you aren't our child, we still love you."

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: But I knew that was impossible. Their own human child was out there somewhere, as were my fae parents. Our family was a lie — and all lies unravel with time.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: So, even though I was terrified, and even though I knew I might end up an unwanted child, I eventually mustered the courage to tell them.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: I did what I thought was right. I knew things might not turn out how I hoped, but I wasn't going back on my decision. The same applies this time — I have to see Celaeno.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Linnea...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Uh... I'm now realizing that I have no idea where she is. Don't tell me I have to wait until the next round of the competition...

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr! Raaaawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Aguara, do you know where Celaeno is?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think he wants us to follow...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Do you remember Celaeno's scent? That's amazing! You're the best, Aggie!

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Phew... Alright! I think I'm about ready to do this. No use delaying it any longer — let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: But what about you, Linnea? What's your perspective?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I... I think I see things differently.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: How about we continue this conversation after the tournament? I'd rather give you my answer then.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Alright, just don't get your hopes up about the future... I don't want to see the disappointment tear you apart.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I'll be fine, trust me. Anyway, we'll leave it there for today — see you in the arena!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes!!!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Well done! Keep it up, Aguara!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After all that, Celaeno's staying in the room right next to ours? No wonder Aguara could pick up her scent!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Is anyone there?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: ...You're sure this is the right room?

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Celaeno, I know you're in there. Please, I need to talk to you!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Celaeno...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I'm not here!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Are too!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Am not! Quit bothering me!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Not a chance! If you don't open the door, I'll be waiting right here outside until you change your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I have so many questions to ask you. Can you at least answer this one? Who are you to me? Are you... Are you my sister?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: OPEN THE DOOR!!!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Alright, stop yelling.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: ...Come in.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hehe, that wasn't so hard now, was it?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Take a seat. Just to be clear, I wasn't expecting visitors, so I can't offer you much in the way of comfort.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Curiosity is a dangerous trait, Linnea. You're gonna regret coming here — don't say I didn't warn you.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You sure about that? 'Cause if I hadn't come here, I'd be regretting it already.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Will you please answer me now? Why do we have the same wings on our heads? Why did I pass out when I touched you? And why did I see all those... those...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: ...Visions of your future?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... it wasn't a dream after all?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Of course not.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Linnea, you're an avid student of the natural world. Surely you're aware of the six most common types of fae?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The Vila, Domovoy, Leshy, Volkodlak, Snegovik, and Jack Frosts.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Right. Well, there are many less common varieties, too. The legendary Lantern Fae, the Sirens with their lilting songs... and us, the "Augury Birds."

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: "We foretell both disaster and delight, gazing upon the past dawn and future night. Others fear and revere our might, while we alone detest our plight."

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: ...I've never heard of an Augury Bird before. Or the poem you just recited.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: That's hardly a surprise. You can count the number of Augury Birds alive today on one hand — and that includes you and me.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: So it's true then... We really are family.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Family... Huh.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Celaeno didn't deny that they're family, but something about that word seems to trigger her. Clearly, she has conflicting emotions about her family.)

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Augury Birds are born with a peculiar ability — we can see "crossroads in the flow of fate." Immutable future events that all paths will lead to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you talking about... prophecies?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've met other people with the ability to see the future.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Doesn't surprise me. Humanity has many ways of observing fate — the stars, the Ley Lines... Our abilities are feeble in comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: We can only see our own fates. If a friend wants to know their future, or someone is concerned about the destiny of the world, we're powerless to help.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: But the way it feels to witness your own fate... I trust you understand by now, Linnea.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It certainly wasn't fun. Those prophecies brought a flood of emotions with them, from excitement, to frustration, to bitterness... By the end, all I was left with was a kind of numb emptiness.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I had a goal in life... and before I even had the chance to start fighting for it, I saw how it would end. *sigh*... It's like someone spoiled the ending of a story I was really enjoying.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Wait till you've tried to defy fate and found how powerless you are to change it... That's when the real suffering begins.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Everything is transpiring as I foresaw, yet I am powerless to change it... Fate is an immutable force. I can but lament as the inevitable unfolds.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: I do wonder whether giving a man the power to see the future does nothing more for him than slowly crush his spirits...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (..."The Visionary" Vedrfolnir once said something similar.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If fate were easier to change, seeing the future would be a huge blessing. It would be a power desired by all.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But... if fate is set in stone, then knowing the future must be a heavy burden to bear.)

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: When you know every joy and every sorrow you'll ever experience, and there's nothing you can do to change it... Like you said, it leaves you with a numb emptiness.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Generation after generation of Augury Birds lived with this burden... until you were born, and our parents found the only solution they could think of.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: "If an Augury Bird is sent far from the fae to grow up among humans, the awakening of their prophetic abilities can be delayed."

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: So that's how I became a changeling.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: What about the child I was switched with？ What happened to her?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Don't worry, she had the opposite problem to you — she needed to live among the fae. She was born with a strange, rare disease that humans cannot cure. If she hadn't been switched, she would have died a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Our parents saved her life, then raised her as their own. Eventually, her birth parents came to find her, and now they're living together in Snezhnograd.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: ...I see. Wow.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It all makes sense now. But there's still one thing you haven't explained... Those things you said before I fainted — what did you mean by all that?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I meant exactly what I said. I don't like you.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: But why?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: No reason.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: So we're back to this? If you won't tell me, I'll have to guess myself.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Celaeno... A—Are you jealous of me?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Hah, good guess. But I wouldn't call it jealousy — more like resentment.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: By the time our parents came up with a solution for you and sent you off to live with the humans, I was already tormented by visions. If I'd been born just a few years later... *sigh* How cruel fate can be.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Mom and Dad would sneak over to Nod-Krai to see you sometimes. They talked about you non-stop. Even that human child got more attention than me.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I came with them once to Nod-Krai. When I saw you there in the distance, living your carefree life... I was torn apart by jealousy, but I had to pretend that nothing was wrong — even that I wished you well.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Did no one ever consider how I felt? What was I to them — a reject? A failure? A pitiful wretch abandoned by fate?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Celaeno...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: All of this led to me deciding, a long time ago, that when you were old enough, I'd come pay you a visit. My plan was to tell you the truth about everything. And then... you would share in my suffering.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I know — what kind of horrible person would want to do that to someone? Someone like me, apparently.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Then why did you hide from me?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You really want me to keep guessing?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: ...It was because I found out the image of you I'd built up in my head — of happy-go-lucky Linnea, spoiled by her parents and coddled by fate — it was all just a fantasy.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I overheard you in Speranza, talking about your past... desperately trying to hide the truth about who you were, somehow getting by with a rag-tag bunch of kids in the Conch Gang.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: You described it so nonchalantly, but it was eating me up inside.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: In that moment, I didn't want to see you suffer... And I couldn't go on resenting you any longer. I just wanted to hold you tight and tell you everything will be fine, that you still have a family...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hey, Sis...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You're really not cut out to be a villain.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: So much for making me suffer, huh? Now you're the one crying, and I have to comfort you!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: But I understand now. That feeling you had? It wasn't resentment... You were just lonely.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I've always wondered about my real family... I'm so glad you were willing to see me, Sis.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Thank you... all of you. This is not how I expected this to go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks it's always best to get everything off your chest. That way, everyone can go back to being happy.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hehe, you're right, Paimon. I haven't been this happy in a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hey, Celaeno, I was wondering... How did you end up with a Radiant Bladehorn as your partner? All the ones I've seen in the wild have been hyper-aggressive. They certainly wouldn't let me get close enough to touch them.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: We met that time when Mom and Dad brought me to see you in Nod-Krai. Haemus was still a baby then — must've gotten separated from his parents. I ended up looking after him for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I suppose our friendship was pre-ordained. Just like my upcoming victory in this competition — an immutable crossroads in the flow of fate.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: "Immutable"?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: You're welcome to try to fight it if you want. Prepare to experience just how cruel fate can be.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Leave this competition and fly somewhere far away. I promise you, something will happen to force you right back here.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Or if you prefer, you could go all out and try to beat me. But I have both luck and superior strength on my side. It's a gulf you will never overcome.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: The prophecies we see are the meeting points of every possible path. There are many possible roads into the future, but they all lead to the same destination in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Now that I know the pain of seeing my own fate for myself, I have to ask... How have you kept going all these years?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I learned to submit to fate. I just have to accept what will happen — there's no other choice.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Since the outcome can't be changed, how I get there doesn't matter in the grand scheme of things. Every crossroad I've foreseen is a curse, so the best I can do is chase a little happiness in the unknowns between them.

talks.objective: Return to your room in The Flagship to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... are you awake?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Neither can Paimon... Linnea and Celaeno aren't the only ones with a big day tomorrow — you've got your semifinal match, too. We have no idea who your opponent could be, and Paimon's a little nervous...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since we're both struggling to sleep, d'you wanna head out for a stroll? We could go grab something yummy, then take Aguara to check out the arena. Might be a good chance for our little warrior to get familiar with the lay of the land.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Listen up, Lumi. I've seen Celaeno's Radiant Bladehorn in action, and it isn't just strong — it's fast, too.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Her best way to exploit both of these traits will be to make her Radiant Bladehorn charge you. You'll have to find a way to dodge the attacks, then pick the right moment to counterattack...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Linnea!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Getting in some last-minute preparation?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Sure am! What are you guys doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Lumi and I were just going over our strategy for tomorrow! Since you're here too, how about letting Aguara join Lumi in some friendly sparring?

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Lure the enemy in and wait for an opening to strike... Yeah, looks like that's my best shot at victory.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: But Haemus is so powerful. Even if we do find an opening, I'm not sure Lumi's even strong enough to make it count. I need a better plan...

choices.text: You've prepared as thoroughly as you can.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Thanks. Just because I've seen a future where I fail doesn't mean I'm willing to go down without a fight!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Fate is such a mysterious idea... Despite having it explained to me and having seen it with my own eyes, I still find it hard to wrap my head around it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What does fate mean to you?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Hmm? You're in a philosophical mood, huh? Well... I dunno if I'm the best person to ask. I've only just learned who I really am — I need some time to think.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Besides, I'm an advisor, remember? It wouldn't be very professional for me to start spouting best-guesses and speculation. What if I led you in the wrong direction?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Relax. I'm just curious to hear your opinion.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Alright, well... I think that knowing the future is a pretty lousy deal. But then, life's full of lousy situations.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: When I was a kid, my greatest suffering came from not knowing. I didn't know how my parents would react when I told them the truth, I didn't know where to go when they left...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Back then, I actually wanted to know the future. I dreamed of a day that fate would send me a sign... I just wanted some clear guidance on what I should do — something to give me the courage to go on.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: But fate didn't show me anything. It was my own stubborn will that got me through. Turned out that the only person I could rely on was me.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: ...I've always known what it's like to be terrified of the unknown, and now I'm learning that knowing for sure isn't all it's cracked up to be, either. What's the big deal? The world hasn't ended, and I haven't changed. What do I have to fear?

response.speaker: Lumi
response.text: Ya-ho!

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Training session over! Feels like these two are really forming a close bond.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Alright! I think we're as prepared as we can be. Time to get some shuteye.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Tomorrow, we're gonna face our fate.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Haemus seems to be running out of steam, but Aguara's already panting too...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like it's time to end this!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aguara, just like we practiced!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Czeslawa
dialogues.text: Is everybody ready!? Prepare yourselves for the opening match of the semifinals!

dialogues.speaker: Czeslawa
dialogues.text: #Our contestants are ready and raring to go! On the one side, we have {NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} partner Aguara, and on the other, we have Viliana and her partner Gorynishche!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can do it, Aguara!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Perhaps because of the last-minute training yesterday, Aguara is more fired up than usual and wins the match with style.

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Czeslawa
dialogues.text: We have a winner! Everyone, please take a short break. The second semifinal will begin shortly!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great job, Aguara!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey {NICKNAME}, Linnea and Celaeno are up next! Come on, let's cheer them on!

dialogues.speaker: Czeslawa
dialogues.text: Looks like our contestants and their partners are in position.

dialogues.speaker: Czeslawa
dialogues.text: On the one side, we have Linnea and her partner Lumi, and on the other side, we have Celaeno and her partner Haemus! Buckle up folks — the semi-finals are about to begin!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: You can do it, old boss!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Go get 'em, Linnea!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Lumi...

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You were amazing! I didn't know you could grow that big!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-hoho...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You know, you look a little different after absorbing all that Geo... Wait a sec! Could that be it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: L—Linnea! Are you guys alright?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, come quick!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I've figured out why Lumi is different from other Jack Frosts! After all the theories I've looked into, it turns out there was one possibility that never even occurred to me.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: What if Lumi wasn't born different at all? What if it's all a consequence of her diet? Surely, ingesting large amounts of rare ore could explain the development of her Geo features...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I mean, just look at vishaps! Depending on their element, vishaps can look wildly different, but from a biological perspective, they're still considered the same species.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Lumi, you don't have to wait for evolution to catch up at all. You just have to find another Jack Frost who likes the same things as you do — then you'll have a true companion!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I'm so happy you unleashed your full power, Lumi. If you hadn't pushed yourself like that, I never would've had this Eureka moment!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I thought Linnea would be disappointed after losing her match... but I guess this reaction is more her style.)

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Linnea...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Why did you hold back?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: What do you mean? If Lumi had landed that hit, you and Haemus would have been in serious danger.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Even so...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: (When that hammer started to fall, the future I once saw went blank before my eyes...)

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: (Did fear cause me to see a false vision? Or did she truly cheat fate for a brief moment?)

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: (...What does it matter? In the end, the pull of fate exerted its force all the same. The prophecy came to pass, as surely as the sun rises in the morning.)

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: What's on your mind, Sis?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I... I just think it's a shame. You gave your all in that battle, but it didn't change a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Whatever path you take, it always leads to the same place. Fate is so cruel.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Celaeno, do you remember the question that you asked me? I told you I'd give you my answer after the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I remember. And I'd still like to know what you think.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You told me, "there are many possible roads into the future, but they all lead to the same destination in the end." Well, I prefer to think of it the other way around: We might already know where we're headed, but we get to choose how we get there.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Maybe fate will always lead us toward the same destination, but I never cared much about the outcome — I just want to walk my own path.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: So even if I was destined to lose to you, there was no way I wasn't gonna give it everything I had.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: And even if my ship ends up at the bottom of the ocean, I'm not gonna let that stop me from sailing it to every corner of the world first.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: If all people care about are outcomes, then why doesn't everyone give up on happiness and love? After all, the certainty of death is the one thing that every person knows about their fate.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: But my feelings, my thoughts, everything I've seen... all that exists beyond the reach of fate. They belong to me, and no one else controls them.

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Lumi, sounds like you agree, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-hoho...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Linnea...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: ...Ignorance really is bliss.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Even when we're scared and uncertain, it's important to face the truth head-on.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You sure about that? 'Cause if I hadn't come here, I'd be regretting it already.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: (How I envied your cheerful optimism when I first saw you... I thought your happiness was all thanks to your obliviousness to fate.)

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: (Yet, now you've witnessed your fate and experienced failure — and still, you haven't let it drag you down.)

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: (Perhaps I was wrong from the start... The difference between us was never about knowledge of our destinies — it's about having the courage to accept it.)

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Celaeno, you okay? You're looking pretty zoned out!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Heh... Actually, I was just thinking... I'm happy for you.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I claimed the victory promised to me by fate, and you found your answer — a truth that transcends fate itself.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Sounds like I got the sweeter deal overall. But hey, mine and Lumi's journey isn't over yet!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: So enjoy your victory, Celaeno. But don't get complacent... Otherwise, my partner here might just take it back from you one day.

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr! Raaaawr!

response.speaker: Lumi
response.text: Ya-ho!

response.speaker: Celaeno
response.text: Haha... That little thing?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: That, plus our special bond!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Let's go, partner. This time, it's my turn to help you train!

talks.objective: Go to Natlan to complete the training

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hello Natlan, I'm back! Give me a moment to set up the tent. I bought this one the last time I was here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! We'll lend you a hand!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Now then, Aggie, it's time for you to learn one of Lumi's signature finishers.

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rrrawr?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Watch closely. Lumi, do the honors!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a rock hammer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh... Linnea, do you seriously think Aguara can use a giant Geo hammer?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: From what I've seen, Aguara's fighting style isn't that dissimilar to Lumi's. They both use agility to set up their opponents while searching for opportunities to attack.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: But Aguara isn't strong enough to break through Haemus's defenses. He needs a weapon to level the playing field.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Aguara will need to channel Geo essence from the ground and fashion it into a powerful rock hammer. Simple enough in principle, but it might take some time to master. Aguara, wanna try it out?

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Don't worry. It's normal to fail on the first try. Just gotta keep trying.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You'll get the hang of it! Lumi, it's up to you to show Aguara how it's done.

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-hoho...

talks.objective: Wait until the evening of the day after tomorrow

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Phew... Feels like I blinked and two whole days went by.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I've heard it said that people can find their fates by studying the stars... I guess that means that fate's been looking down on us this whole time, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: *yawn*... I could really do with some sleep. Good night, you guys.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (As a Descender, my fate is my own. I don't know what it's like to have my destiny anchored in place.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The rules of this world surely exist for a good reason, and the same must go for fate. But on this journey, I've witnessed far too many people who yearn to defy their fate.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is anchoring fate in place truly the best solution? Maybe one day, I can—)

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr...

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr...
Rawr.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Paimon slept really well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Whoa, look at all this Grainfruit! Aguara, did you pick these for us?

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! When did you learn to do that!?

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Are you saying... you had help from another saurian? Hmm, who could that be?

talks.objective: Return to the Frostmoon Enclave to complete the finals

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Now, Haemus. Trample him!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: March to victory, and leave nothing standing.

talks.objective: Return to the Frostmoon Enclave to complete the finals

dialogues.speaker: Slawomir
dialogues.text: ...Haemus has lost the strength to fight on! It's all over folks! The champions are —

dialogues.speaker: Slawomir
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} partner Aguara!

dialogues.speaker: A Seat in the Audience
dialogues.text: Aguara! Aguara!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: So, I lost...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: You did superbly, Haemus. Get some good rest.

dialogues.speaker: Haemus
dialogues.text: Raargh...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Seems I underestimated your little partner. I'm impressed.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hehe, what did I say? Told you my partner would help me settle the score.

choices.text: You played a big part in this win!

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Lumi
response.text: Ya-ho!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we will now take a short break to give our finalists a moment to recover. But don't go too far, because we'll be back very soon for the awards ceremony!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Thank you to all our contestants for your amazing performances! Now, we'll be interviewing our four top finishers!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: #First up, it's our champions, {NICKNAME} and Aguara!

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: We can all see that Aguara is still a young slip of a tepetlisaur, and yet the fiercest of enemies couldn't stand in his way. So tell us, what's the secret to Aguara's success?

choices.text: The secret is Aguara's special connections with his friends.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: I see. It sounds like behind every champion is a dedicated group of supportive friends.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: I'm sure we're all looking forward to even more spectacular performances from Aguara in the future. Do you think you're up for the challenge, little one?

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Next, we have our runner-up, Celaeno. Let me start by asking, what's next for you and Haemus? Will the two of you keep adventuring together in the future?

response.speaker: Celaeno
response.text: ...No. Haemus doesn't belong with me. I'm hoping that soon, I can set him free to roam the wild.

response.speaker: Celaeno
response.text: And of course... Since he's so friendly towards humans, I do hope any adventurers who run into Haemus in the future won't mistreat him.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Sounds like Haemus is a real freedom-lover. If we have any adventurers in the crowd, please keep your eyes peeled and make sure not to hurt our friendly Radiant Bladehorn.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Moving on now, we have some more familiar faces from the semifinals.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: This first question is for Linnea. During your match against Celaeno, you jumped in to stop your own partner Lumi's rampage, costing you a certain victory. Do you have any regrets?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: I'd be lying if I said I didn't regret it even a little bit...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: But who wouldn't? All we can do is live our best life and hope to look back with as few regrets as possible.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: And overall, I had a really great time in this competition! I've found my long-lost family, and we really care about one another.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Inspiring words from Linnea. Now it's time for our final interviewee — please welcome Viliana, from Snezhnograd. Anything you'd like to share with the crowd?

response.speaker: Viliana
response.text: Well, I've been really loving Nod-Krai. There's so much to see and do! I'm planning to stick around for a while, so if you see me around, come and say hey!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Great, enjoy your stay, Viliana! Well folks, we've heard from all four of our semifinalists. Now, to round things off, it's time for a group photo!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Thank you to everyone who took part in the "Spirit Envoy Championship." We hope to see you next time!

choices.text: The secret is hard work and practice.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: I see. Well, it seems like an indomitable will helped Aguara achieve the impossible.

choices.text: It was all thanks to Lumi's secret weapon.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Linnea, I gotta get going. I'll make sure to tell Mom and Dad how you're doing — I know they'll be so happy for you.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Without me around, your prophetic abilities will be slow to develop. But you should know that since you've been to the tundra, and you've encountered others of your kind, it's only a matter of time before your abilities fully awaken.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I'm sure you already know how I'm going to respond, Sis. I'm not afraid to know the future — all that scares me is the prospect of a life without you, Mom, and Dad.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: I know. Well, write me whenever you want to see me — I'll be there in a heartbeat.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: And when you're ready, come visit us in the tundra. I'll give you the address.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Thanks, Celaeno. I can't wait to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: People seem to really dig the drinks here! I wonder if I should take some back for Granny Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It's getting pretty late. We should all get some sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh...? The Flagship? What're we doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: So, Aguara comes from Natlan, right?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: If we're gonna train hard, we should do it there. There's plenty of natural Phlogiston around, which will help keep the little one's stamina up.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You're staying at The Flagship too, right? No need to see me out, I'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Oh, and thanks so much for keeping me company today! Hehe. Good night!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Hiding underground, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Keep charging, Haemus. Jolt him out of the hole!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Tch... Haemus, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Haemus
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: ...Predictable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aguara hit him right in the belly... But it didn't seem to do anything.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: It was the obvious move. Haemus was well-prepared for an attack like that.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Wait! Aguara's horn hasn't finished growing yet...

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Voitto
dialogues.text: The final is about to begin. Contestants, please take your positions. Spectators, we kindly ask you to wait outside the arena.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's finally here! Aguara, today's your time to shine!

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It's all up to you now, partner. You've done the hard yards in training, now go out there and believe in yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It's time to write your name in lights and show the world how hard we've worked. You've got this, Aguara!

response.speaker: Lumi
response.text: Ya-hoho...

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Ladies and gentlemen, the wait is finally over! It's time for the Spirit Envoy Championship final!

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: You'll be very familiar with our contestants by now. Celaeno and her partner, the Radiant Bladehorn, Haemus, who seized their place in the final after a hard-won victory in the last round.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: #Then we have {NICKNAME} and Aguara. This little Tepetlisaur might not look like the most ferocious beast, but this duo have fought courageously to reach the final stage.

response.speaker: Czeslawa
response.text: Who will be crowned champions today? In a few short moments, we will find out!

response.speaker: Celaeno
response.text: Back from training camp?

response.speaker: Aguara
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Celaeno
response.text: Then let's do this. Show me what you've got.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: You've got this, Aguara, don't be nervous!

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Still hoping for an opening?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Don't give him time to think, Haemus.

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Has fear robbed you of all reason?

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Haemus, stamp down with all your might.

dialogues.speaker: Aguara
dialogues.text: Rawr...

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Mm... Impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: Haemus, summon Anemo energy on your horn and then charge.

dialogues.speaker: Celaeno
dialogues.text: ...Now you see what you're up against.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You'll get the hang of it! Lumi, it's up to you to show Aguara how it's done.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Now that Aguara's mastered Lumi's secret weapon, it's time to head back to Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we should get back just in time for the finals!
